text.stageNote: In process order, from the dock door to the customer.
tips: The stage is where the damage was seen, the cause is why it happened. Both matter.
Six crushed parcels from one collapsed wall are six units.
Without units handled you see counts; with them you get a rate, DPMO and sigma level.
text.checkIntro: Walk the dock and tick what you actually see today, not what the SOP says. Every unticked line is a place where damage can start.

Receiving.meaning: Much of what is found at receiving arrived damaged. If it is not recorded at the door, your site pays for someone else's damage.
moves: Inspect and photograph damaged pallets before signing, and note it on the delivery note.
Keep "arrived damaged" separate from "damaged here" in the log.
Share the numbers with the supplier or carrier every week, with photos.
Receiving.question: Who checks the goods before the delivery note is signed?

Storage.meaning: Damage while goods sit still points to racking, height, water or traffic around the location.
moves: Store heavy items low and check that nothing overhangs the beam or shelf edge.
Look where damage clusters: aisle ends, corners and forklift turns usually need protection.
Walk the building for water: roof leaks, condensation, doors left open in rain.
Storage.question: Which locations keep producing damage, and what passes by them?

Picking.meaning: Items are dropped, pulled from under other items or thrown into totes when picking is rushed or the location is awkward.
moves: Watch ten picks at the worst location and note how the item is taken out.
Move heavy and fragile items to waist height where they are picked often.
Heavy first, fragile last: set the pick order so nothing heavy lands on top.
Picking.question: What does a picker have to do to take this item out safely?

Packing.meaning: Wrong box size, too little void fill or weak tape. The parcel leaves looking fine and fails on the way.
moves: Agree a box size per item group and keep those boxes at the station.
Shake test: if the item moves inside the box, add fill before closing it.
Flag fragile items in the system so the packer sees it before packing.
Packing.question: What does the packer do when the right box is not at the station?

Loading.meaning: Most transport damage is created at the moment the vehicle is loaded: stacking order, gaps, speed at peak time.
moves: Heavy at the bottom, light on top, fragile never under anything.
Build stable walls with no gaps or overhang, and secure the last wall before the doors close.
Check peak loading slots: when the loading-time target wins over the stacking standard, damage follows.
Loading.question: What does the load look like in the last ten minutes before departure?

Transport.meaning: The load moves in the vehicle: braking, turns, missing load securing, shelving that does not hold.
moves: Check load securing before departure and take one photo of the closed load.
Compare damage by route, vehicle and driver before blaming the road.
Repair shelving, straps and securing points in the vehicles that show up most.
Transport.question: Does the load look the same at the first stop as it did at departure?

Handover.meaning: Damage in the last metres: parcels thrown, left in the rain or put down in unsafe places.
moves: Carry, never throw: two hands for the last metres.
Protect parcels from rain at the door with a bag or a cover.
Take a photo at handover so damage claims can be checked fairly.
Handover.question: What happens to a parcel between the vehicle door and the customer?

causes.Stacking: Write the stacking rule as one picture at the dock: heavy low, fragile high, no gaps.
causes.Handling: Watch the work at the busiest hour. Handling damage grows when people are rushed, not when they are careless.
causes.Packaging: Test the packaging, not the people: drop and shake one parcel of each type that shows up here.
causes.Equipment: Check forks, pallet trucks, cages and roll containers. Take broken equipment out of use the same day.
causes.Load securing: Make securing the last step of loading, with a photo, not something the driver has to remember.
causes.Environment: Water, heat and cold damage goods silently. Close the gaps: doors, roofs, covers, waiting areas.
causes.Unknown: A large Unknown share means the log is not yet good enough. Record stage and cause at the moment damage is found.

checklist: Heavy items go at the bottom, light and fragile items on top.
Nothing overhangs the pallet, shelf or cage edge.
Walls are stable, with no gaps a parcel can fall into.
The load is secured with straps, bars or nets before the doors close.
Fragile items and liquids are marked and travel upright.
Damaged boxes are taken out and repacked, never loaded as they are.
Forks, pallet trucks and cages are checked before use.
Leaks, wet floors and open doors near goods are reported the same shift.
Every damage is logged with stage and cause at the moment it is found.
Goods that arrive damaged are photographed and noted before signing.
